findings.title: Invalidation-on-update decision uses the org-aware wrapped model as the 'original'
findings.body: `update()` takes `idpById = getById(...)`, which returns the anonymous org-aware wrapper. Its `isEnabled()` also depends on whether the organization and the organization feature are enabled. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` evaluates `getLoginPredicate()` on this wrapper, so `test(original)` can be false even though the IDP is stored as enabled and is present in the cached login list (the cache is filled from the DB, where only the IDP's own `enabled` counts). Example: the org is disabled, the IDP is stored enabled, and an admin sets it to disabled. Both `test(original)` and `test(updated)` are false, so the early return skips invalidation. The cached login list still holds the now-disabled IDP, and callers other than the login bean (which re-checks `isEnabled`) see a stale entry. Evaluate the predicate on the raw stored model (for example `idpDelegate.getById`), or always invalidate when the org-aware wrapper is involved.

findings.title: Per-organization search keys bloat and thrash a single cache entry per fetch mode
findings.body: All searches for a fetch mode share one `IdentityProviderListQuery` entry, and `searchKey` is the organizationId. For `REALM_ONLY` the delegate ignores organizationId, so the same result is stored once per org. For `ALL`, every organization's set repeats all realm-level login IDPs. Each first lookup for a new org takes the `cached == null` branch, which calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and rebuilds a new query by copying all previous searches. In a realm with many organizations this means O(orgs) growth of one entry, O(n²) copying, and repeated local invalidation/re-adds on the hot login path. Normalise the key (use `""` for `REALM_ONLY`) and/or key the entry by organization instead of piling everything into one query.

findings.title: remove() now always hits the DB even when the IDP is in the cache
findings.body: `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` runs unconditionally. Before, the DB lookup only happened when the alias key was already invalidated in this transaction; otherwise the cached entry was used. The result is only needed to evaluate the login predicate, so every removal now pays an extra query. Reuse the cached model (`cached.getIdentityProvider()`) when available, and only fall back to the delegate when the entry is missing or invalid.

findings.title: Cleanup removes the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP named "alias", not the one created in the loop (`idp-alias-N`). The same applies to the cleanup for `idp-alias-20` at line 425. The created providers are never cleaned up, and the cleanup call either fails with a 404 or is silently ignored. Leftover IDPs can leak into other tests that share the realm. Use the actual alias variable.

findings.title: Test checks only cache presence, never the returned results or invalidation on creating/removing an eligible IDP
findings.body: `testCacheIDPForLogin` inspects the `IdentityProviderListQuery` contents but never asserts what `getForLogin` actually returns on a cache hit (including the wrapped, org-aware models and the HashSet reassembly). It only covers creating a non-eligible IDP and removing a non-eligible IDP, so the branches that matter are untested. These are: creating an eligible IDP, removing an eligible IDP (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation` in `create`/`remove`), disabling an eligible IDP, and organization disable/enable. A regression in those invalidation paths would go unnoticed.
